title: Scaffold-supported Transplantation of Islets in the Epididymal Fat Pad of Diabetic Mice
protocol: Reconstitute collagenase P powder in HBSS to make a 5 mg/mL solution.
Filter the reconstituted collagenase P solution through a 0.22 µm filter.
Aliquot 0.6 mL of filtered collagenase P solution into 15-mL conical tubes and store at -20°C.
Dilute each aliquot with HBSS to prepare 6 mL working solutions at 0.5 mg/mL concentration.
Keep the diluted working solution on ice for immediate use within 1 hour.
Prepare neutralization solution by adding FBS (2.5%) and P/S (1%) into HBSS.
Store the neutralization solution on ice.
Autoclave surgery instruments at 115°C for 30 minutes under 15 psi pressure.
Prepare 12 mL of collagenase working solution for 6 mice.
Fill a 10 mL syringe with 9 mL of prepared collagenase working solution.
Connect the filled syringe to a 27 G intravenous needle.
Store the syringe on ice and use within 1 hour.
Euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation.
Place the mouse in supine position on a paper towel with the tail pointing towards the operator.
Spray the whole body with 70% ethanol to make it completely wet.
Make a V-incision starting from the genital area and extending to the diaphragm using dissection scissors and forceps.
Fold the skin over the chest to completely reveal the abdominal cavity.
Move the bowel to the right side of the mouse and expose the pancreas and common bile duct.
Grab the duodenum carefully with forceps and pull it until the bile duct is taut.
Find the portal vein and bile duct leading into the liver.
Clamp the portal vein and bile duct with a microscopic hemostatic clamp.
Hold the intestine with the forceps and find the location of the ampulla that connects the bile duct and the duodenum.
Insert a 27G intravenous needle into the common bile duct through the ampulla.
Dispense about 200 μL of collagenase working solution to check if the cannulation is all the way through the bile duct.
If the collagenase solution begins to fill the duct, clamp the duct segment containing the needle using an artery hemostatic clamp.
Dispense the rest of the 2 mL of collagenase solution at a slow and constant rate within 1 min.
Push the bowel to the left side of the mouse and remove the pancreas starting from the descending colon.
Lift the bowel using forceps and separate it from the pancreas with another pair of forceps.
Continue removing the pancreas until it is unattached from the top of the stomach.
Lift the pancreas out of the abdomen and cut it free from the remaining spleen.
Place the pancreas in an empty 15-mL conical tube on ice.
Incubate the conical tubes containing the perfused pancreas at 37°C for 17 minutes.
Terminate the digestion by adding 7 mL of neutralization solution and placing the tubes on ice.
Shake the tubes vigorously (e.g., 20 times in 10 seconds) until fine tissue particles are obtained.
Filter the digested tissue samples through a 0.5-mm wire mesh to remove non-digested tissue chunks.
Collect the islet suspensions in a new 50-mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the tubes for 3 minutes at 230 x g and 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant carefully, without disturbing the tissue pellets.
Resuspend the pellets from 3 mice in 4 mL of polysucrose density gradient by vortexing gently or pipetting up and down a few times.
Slowly pipette 4 mL of HBSS down the side of the tube to the top of the polysucrose solutions.
Centrifuge the suspension for 20 minutes at 900 x g and 4°C using a very slow acceleration rate.
End the centrifugation with no brake.
Remove the entirety of the 8-mL supernatant solutions using a large-bore 15-mL pipette.
Pass the solutions through an inverted 70-µm strainer.
Pipette 2 mL of cold neutralization solution into a 35-mm Petri dish.
Invert the cell strainer right-side-up and dip the surface retaining the islets in the solution, gently shaking to release the islets.
Hand-pick the islets under a microscope using a 20-µL pipette with a white tip.
Place about 200 islets in a 35-mm dish with 2 mL of culture medium.
Incubate at 37 °C in an incubator supplied with 5% CO2 for 12 h.
Shake the suspension well to evenly distribute the islets in the dish and reduce clumping.
Cut DCS scaffolds into 7-mm disks.
Soak scaffolds in 70% ethanol.
Wash scaffolds with HBSS.
Place scaffolds in 24-well tissue culture inserts.
Swirl the dish to collect islets from the center using a 20 μL pipette with a white tip.
Transfer 250 islets per scaffold using a pipette.
Add 2 mL of culture medium to the well containing the scaffolds and islets.
Culture the islets for 12 h before transplantation.
Place C57BL/6J mice in a fresh cage with water but no food.
Fast the mice for 10 h before diabetes induction.
Mix 0.1 M citric acid with 0.1 M sodium citrate to prepare buffer solutions with pH values of 4.2-4.5.
Dissolve STZ (10 mg/mL) in the freshly prepared buffer solution.
Sterilize the STZ solution by passing it through a 0.22 μm filter.
Prepare fresh STZ solution right before injection.
Inject each mouse intraperitoneally with STZ at a dose of 140-150 mg/kg for C57BL/6J mice.
Collect tail vein blood and monitor blood glucose on days 2, 3, and 4 post-STZ injection.
Anesthetize the mice with pentobarbital delivered intraperitoneally (50 mg/kg).
Place the mouse in a supine position on a paper towel with the tail pointing towards the operator.
Shave the abdomen extensively to remove fur from around the incision site.
Tape down the four limbs of the mouse.
Swab the skin completely with alternating alcohol and iodophor wipes moved in a circular fashion.
Drape the mouse with a sterile drape, only allowing access to the incision area.
Make a 7 mm incision through the peritoneal wall in the midline close to the genital area.
Gently grab and remove the EFP from the abdominal cavity using forceps.
Spread the EFP on wetted sterile gauze.
Place the scaffold containing islets on the EFP and fold the EFP to wrap the transplant.
Secure direct contact between the islets and EFP by suturing the EFP with absorbable 6-0 sutures.
Wet the surface of the EFP with sterile saline using a soaked cotton swab.
Gently place the EFP back in the abdominal cavity.
Close the incision by suturing the peritoneal wall.
Clamp the dermal layer with wound clips.
Inject buprenorphine (0.1 mg/kg) subcutaneously as an analgesic.
Inject 1 mL of saline subcutaneously to prevent dehydration.
Place the mouse in a cage on a heating pad until the mouse recovers from anesthesia.
Check non-fasting glucose levels two days later by collecting blood from the tail vein.
If retrieving the graft, gently pull out the EFP.
Use 3-0 suture to ligate the end of the fat pad adjacent to the epididymis.
Occlude the blood vessels.
Explant the EFP graft and preserve it for histology.
